extracted.intended_audience: journalists, reporters and editors (news organizations, copy editors)
extracted.subtask_description: A Reuters general style guide covering word usage, capitalization, hyphenation, definitions and reporting cautions used by journalists and editors when writing news copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mach number
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Mach number is the ratio of an aircraft’s speed through the air compared with the speed of sound in the same conditions; use Mach 1, Mach 2 etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Madagascar / Malagasy
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Malagasy for the people and the language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Madonna
rubrics_metrics.description: Use this title or 'the Virgin Mary' not 'Our Lady' except in formal titles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'Our Lady of Czestochowa' or names of churches where appropriate; prefer 'the Virgin Mary' otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: madrasa
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to describe an Islamic religious school in some Muslim countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: mafia
rubrics_metrics.description: Lower case unless referring to a specific branch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maghreb
rubrics_metrics.description: Loosely North Africa (less Egypt); literal meaning western part of Middle East; also an official name in Arabic for Morocco.

rubrics_metrics.name: mailman
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'letter carrier' or 'postal worker' (U.S.).

rubrics_metrics.name: maintain
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a verb of saying it can, like 'claim', suggest reporters are sceptical about the statement quoted.

rubrics_metrics.name: major (adjective)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid 'major' as an adjective unless necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not superfluous find a precise alternative. Exception: golf where the four biggest tournaments are called 'the majors'.

rubrics_metrics.name: majority of / vast majority of
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'most' instead of 'majority of' or 'vast majority of'.

rubrics_metrics.name: majority / plurality (election results)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Majority = more than half the votes or more votes than all others combined; plurality = more than the next highest number and may be less than 50 percent. An absolute majority is more than half; relative majority is more votes than anyone else. When used alone, majority and plurality usually take a singular verb.

rubrics_metrics.name: majority leader
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capitalize when used as a formal title (e.g. Senate Majority Leader Harry Reid).

rubrics_metrics.name: Malagasy
rubrics_metrics.description: The people or language of Madagascar.

rubrics_metrics.name: man / mankind
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer 'humanity' when referring to the human race.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manila
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lower case for 'paper' and 'envelopes' (e.g., Manila envelope).

rubrics_metrics.name: manoeuvre / maneuver
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'manoeuvre' in British style; 'maneuver' in American style.

rubrics_metrics.name: mantel / mantle
rubrics_metrics.description: Mantel = fireplace frame; mantle = cloak or covering.

rubrics_metrics.name: manufacture / manufacturer
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'make' or 'maker' where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: maps
rubrics_metrics.description: Check distances, directions and place names using a map.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always verify distances and directions given in a story and check place names.

rubrics_metrics.name: marines
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capitalize when referring to the U.S. Marine Corps or its members (e.g., Six U.S. Marines). Do not refer to them as 'soldiers'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marseille
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'Marseille, France'.

rubrics_metrics.name: marshal / marshalling
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marshal is an official in charge of ceremonies or military affairs (e.g., field marshal). 'Marshall' appears in proper names (Marshall Plan, Marshall Islands). Do not confuse with 'martial' (relating to war).

rubrics_metrics.name: Masters Series
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capitalise and use no apostrophe (e.g., Rome Masters Series tournament).

rubrics_metrics.name: Masters Tournament
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No apostrophe; call it 'the Masters' on second reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: masterful / masterly
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Masterly' = very skilful; 'masterful' = imperious or domineering. Use 'masterly' for skilful displays and 'masterful' for domineering behaviour.

rubrics_metrics.name: match point
rubrics_metrics.description: Two words in tennis and racket sports scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: materiel
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the English term for military equipment.

rubrics_metrics.name: materialise
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless you mean 'take bodily form' prefer 'happen', 'occur' or 'take place'.

rubrics_metrics.name: may / can
rubrics_metrics.description: Different meanings and caution on headlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'May' is about permission or uncertainty; 'can' is about ability. Using 'may' in headlines is overdone.

rubrics_metrics.name: may / might
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In past tense 'may' implies continued uncertainty; 'might' implies a possibility which did not happen.

rubrics_metrics.name: May Day / mayday
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capitalize 'May Day' for the holiday; 'mayday' is the distress call for ships and aircraft.

rubrics_metrics.name: mayoress
rubrics_metrics.description: Use for the wife of a mayor, not a female mayor.

rubrics_metrics.name: McDonnell Douglas Corp
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not 'MacDonnell' or 'McDonnell-Douglas' for the U.S. aircraft company.

rubrics_metrics.name: M.D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'doctor', 'physician' or 'surgeon' instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: meagre / meager
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'meagre' in British style, 'meager' in American.

rubrics_metrics.name: mean (statistics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify which 'mean' you mean: arithmetic average, median or mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the word 'average' where it correctly qualifies the item intended. Explain types if necessary (arithmetic mean, middle value, most commonly occurring value).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mecca
rubrics_metrics.description: One of Islam's Holy Places; avoid colloquial use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use 'Mecca' in a colloquial sense (e.g., 'tourist mecca') since that is disparaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: measures (metric abbreviations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use singular form without full stop for metric units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'kg' or 'km' not 'kgs' or 'kms'. The following need not be spelled out on first mention: kg, km, lb, cm, mm. See also conversions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medal of Honor
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred name for the highest U.S. military honor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not refer to it as the 'Congressional Medal of Honor'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medecins sans Frontieres (MSF)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spell out in first reference, abbreviate to MSF on second reference and translate the name. Take care when saying where MSF is based; branches act independently. See www.msf.org

rubrics_metrics.name: medical stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Handle stories about new health threats or cures with great care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If dramatic claims for cures (e.g., AIDS or cancer) do not come from a reputable named source, check with recognised medical experts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medicaid
rubrics_metrics.description: U.S. federal/state programme to help pay for health care for needy, elderly, blind, disabled and low-income families.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medicare
rubrics_metrics.description: U.S. federal health care insurance program for people 65+ and the disabled.

rubrics_metrics.name: meet / mete
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'met' not 'met with' in many cases; 'mete' means distribute or apportion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: He met party leaders, not 'He met with party leaders.' 'Mete' is to apportion; avoid adjectival 'mete' unless in quotation.

rubrics_metrics.name: mega-
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid mega- as an informal prefix meaning 'very large'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use it only when it means one million.

rubrics_metrics.name: megaton
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A megaton equals the explosive force of one million tons of TNT.

rubrics_metrics.name: megawatt / megawatt-hour
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capacity/output measured in megawatts (MW); cumulative output in megawatt hours (MWh). Do not confuse megawatt (MW) with milliwatt (mW).

rubrics_metrics.name: Melanesia / Micronesia / Polynesia
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Melanesia in the Southwest Pacific, Micronesia north of Melanesia, Polynesia in the central Pacific.

rubrics_metrics.name: men's / women's
rubrics_metrics.description: Use apostrophes for possessives but not in clothing terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'men’s', 'women’s' but 'menswear' and 'womenswear' are one word without apostrophes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Messerschmitt
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not 'Messerschmidt' for the German aircraft company or MBB (Messerschmitt-Boelkow-Bloehm).

rubrics_metrics.name: Messiah
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalise in religious uses; lower case generically.

rubrics_metrics.name: metal / mettle
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Metal' = material like copper or steel. 'Mettle' = spirit, temperament, courage.

rubrics_metrics.name: metaphors
rubrics_metrics.description: Use fresh and vivid metaphors but avoid mixed or absurd ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid mixed metaphors and metaphors whose literal sense is absurd (e.g., don't use two incompatible images).

rubrics_metrics.name: meters (US) vs metres
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'meters' (not 'metres') for gas, electricity and parking meters.

rubrics_metrics.name: metre (spelling / conversions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Spell out 'metre' in full and convert to feet/yards for short distances when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For short distances (up to 10 metres) convert to feet; for longer distances convert to yards. Provide conversion heuristics (roughly add a zero and divide by three) and precise multipliers (1 m = 3.28 ft, 1 m = 1.094 yd). In athletics and swimming results, units may be omitted; in sports reporting, do not convert except for golf and U.S. sport.

rubrics_metrics.name: metric ton / tonne / long ton / short ton
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'ton' and 'tonne' but make clear the kind: tonne = 1,000 kg = 2,204.6 lb; long ton = 2,240 lb; short ton = 2,000 lb (American).

rubrics_metrics.name: mid- prefix
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No hyphen unless the following word starts with a capital (e.g., mid-Pacific). Exceptions include cricket terms (mid-off) and 'midterm' (no hyphen).

rubrics_metrics.name: middle initials in names
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid using middle initials unless essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mideast
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'Middle East'.

rubrics_metrics.name: MiG
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this abbreviation for the aircraft (e.g., MiG-25).

rubrics_metrics.name: mileage
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry exists for usage; check related guidance for miles/mile.

rubrics_metrics.name: mile / conversions
rubrics_metrics.description: Conversion factors and nautical mile definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To convert miles to kilometres multiply by 1.609. One nautical mile = 1.853 km.

rubrics_metrics.name: miles per gallon (mpg)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'mpg' only for second and subsequent references; spell out on first reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: miles per hour (mph)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'mph' only for second and subsequent references; spell out on first reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: militant
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A member of a non-state group who carries arms or believes in using force to achieve aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Military (general guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid military jargon and metaphors; prefer plain English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use jargon unless necessary; avoid terms like 'collateral damage' and 'friendly fire' unless in quotes; know military terms but do not use them to obscure meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aircraft (military reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Terms and definitions related to aircraft coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'air base' (two words), 'air raid' (two words) but 'airspace' and 'airstrike' (one word). AWACS, helicopters, 'stealth' (do not capitalise), STOL, UAV, VTOL definitions and contextual guidance are provided. Prefer to be specific (fighter, bomber) rather than generic 'warplane'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Armoured Vehicles
rubrics_metrics.description: If unsure call it an 'armoured vehicle'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define AFV, APC, tank differences; know when a self-propelled gun may be mistaken for a tank.

rubrics_metrics.name: Battle (terms)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use one word for 'battlefield', 'battlefront', 'battleground'; avoid vague adjectives like 'fierce' or 'heavy' unless casualties or intensity justify them; explain what is meant by 'fighting'. Avoid 'BDA' unless in quotes and spell it out if quoted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Military titles
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ranks should never be abbreviated and should be capitalised when referring to a specific individual (e.g., Lieutenant Colonel). At second reference use surname or rank (e.g., Brown or the general). Follow local practice for hyphenation in countries like Canada and India. Translate non-English ranks without hyphens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ships (naval terms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use precise ship type names and avoid using 'battleship' generically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify vessel class (e.g., frigate, destroyer). 'Warship' implies a combatant; 'battleship' is obsolete. 'Aircraft carrier' defined; 'assault ship' and 'submarine' explained (submarine often called a 'boat').

rubrics_metrics.name: Units and formations
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalisation and definitions for army units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capitalise specific unit titles (e.g., 1st Infantry Division) but otherwise use generic terms (division). Define squad, platoon, company, battalion, brigade, division, corps, army and note national variations; caution with terms like 'regiment' and 'squadron'. Use 'troops' for large round numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weapons (terminology and usage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensive guidance on weapon types, hyphenation, and terminology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hyphenate 'air-to-ground' and similar terms; define artillery, automatic weapon, ballistic missile, bullet vs cartridge, bunker buster, calibre usage, cannon (avoid archaic use), cluster bomb, cruise missile (do not capitalise), Daisy Cutter, e-bomb, gun, howitzer, ICBM, IRBM, machinegun, machine pistol, MIRV, MOAB, mortar (use 'mortar bomb' not 'shell'), multiple-rocket launcher, recoilless rifle, rifle, RPG, sub-machinegun, SAM, SLBM. Avoid vague terms like 'unconventional weapon' — be specific. Spell out WMD on first reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: militate / mitigate
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Militate' means to have force or influence (often 'militate against'); 'mitigate' means to alleviate or moderate.

rubrics_metrics.name: millennium / millennia
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From Latin mille (thousand) and annus (year).

rubrics_metrics.name: millimetre / millimeter
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'millimetre' (British) but 'millimeter' in American style. Use 'mm' with no space, e.g., '30mm cannon'.

rubrics_metrics.name: million (usage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Spell out 'million' in text; use 'mln' in headlines for brevity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use numerals before 'million' (e.g., 6 million). Do not use more than two decimal places.

rubrics_metrics.name: milquetoast
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meaning: a character easily dominated; not 'milk toast'.

rubrics_metrics.name: minimal
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates the least possible size or amount; do not confuse with 'small' or 'tiny'.

rubrics_metrics.name: miracles
rubrics_metrics.description: Use only in religious stories; avoid cliché in disasters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep 'miracles' for religious contexts. In disaster reports avoid clichés such as 'It was a miracle no one was killed.'

rubrics_metrics.name: mob
rubrics_metrics.description: Use with care; avoid for political protests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer neutral 'crowd' unless there is unorganised violence.

rubrics_metrics.name: moderate
rubrics_metrics.description: Use with care; avoid implying a value judgment about Islam or Muslims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mohammad / Muhammad (name spellings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred forms for the Prophet and other individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'Mohammad' for the Prophet and for anyone of this name unless a different spelling is known or appears in an official title. The guide also notes 'Muhammad' entries; follow local/individual preference when known.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monaco
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'Monaco' not 'Monte Carlo' as dateline.

rubrics_metrics.name: money / monies
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'money' rather than 'monies'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mont Blanc
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mont Blanc is 15,771 ft / 4,807 m; highest in western Europe; note Elbrus is highest in Europe if including Caucasus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Montessori
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry exists; use the name as proper noun.

rubrics_metrics.name: months (abbreviations)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abbreviate to Jan., Feb., Aug., Sept., Oct., Nov., Dec. with a full stop when used with a specific date (e.g., Feb. 12); spell out when used alone or with only the year (e.g., February 2002). In datelines and headlines use Jan, Feb, March, April, etc., without full stop.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moonie
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid the pejorative term for members of the Unification Church.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use it in copy and avoid in direct quotations where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: moot
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using 'a moot point' in a quote, explain it as a debatable point.

rubrics_metrics.name: more than / over (numbers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'more than' with numbers and 'over' with less specific quantities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'more than 100' or 'over half.'

rubrics_metrics.name: moribund
rubrics_metrics.description: Meaning: about to die or in a dying state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use to mean weak, stagnant or not growing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mormon
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A member of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints or Mormon Church; 'Latter-day' capitalise only the L. The Church claims about eight million members worldwide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moslem / Muslim
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'Muslim' in all cases; avoid 'Moslem'.

rubrics_metrics.name: mother-in-law
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'mother-in-law' and 'mothers-in-law'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mother's Day
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'Mother’s Day' (not 'Mothers’ Day').

rubrics_metrics.name: mount
rubrics_metrics.description: Give the full name for mountains and communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E.g., 'Mount Everest', 'Mount Vernon'.

rubrics_metrics.name: move (noun)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid 'move' as a noun when possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer 'decision', 'agreement', or another more precise alternative.

rubrics_metrics.name: move to (phrase)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid misleading use of 'move to' when only verbal action occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid phrases that give a spurious sense of physical action when only speech occurred (e.g., 'moved to head off congressional opposition' if only a statement was made).

rubrics_metrics.name: mpg / mph
rubrics_metrics.description: Abbreviations for miles per gallon and miles per hour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both acceptable at second and subsequent references, lower case and without full stops. Spell out on first reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ms
rubrics_metrics.description: Use guidance for forms of address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guide notes 'Ms' as a form like Mr, Mrs, Miss, Master; follow local style — in some contexts not used.

rubrics_metrics.name: mujahideen
rubrics_metrics.description: Term meaning Islamic guerrilla groups or holy warriors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mullah
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Muslim scholar. Often used pejoratively for clerics in Iran; avoid in that context and never use as shorthand for Tehran’s religious-political leadership unless quoting.

rubrics_metrics.name: multi- prefix
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not hyphenate words starting with 'multi'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'multilateral', 'multinational', 'multicultural', 'multilingual' without hyphens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mumbai
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'Mumbai', not 'Bombay', unless in a proper name.

rubrics_metrics.name: murder
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'murder' only for violent deaths without political overtones and generally avoid unless there has been a conviction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Otherwise use 'killing' unless 'murder' is used in a criminal charge or trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Murphy's law
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid the cliché; explain only if used in a quote.

rubrics_metrics.name: mute
rubrics_metrics.description: Use for someone physically unable to speak.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use 'dumb'. Use 'speech impaired' for people who have difficulty speaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: NAACP
rubrics_metrics.description: National Association for the Advancement of Colored Peoples (U.S.).

rubrics_metrics.name: NAFTA
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A trade pact between the United States, Mexico and Canada.

rubrics_metrics.name: names (see cross-references)
rubrics_metrics.description: See entries for personal names, proper names, courtesy titles, nobility, religious titles, royalty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nanjing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'Nanjing, China'.

rubrics_metrics.name: nano-
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefix for one-billionth of a unit.

rubrics_metrics.name: naphtha
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not 'naptha'.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASA
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At first reference a form like 'the U.S. space agency NASA' is acceptable. See www.nasa.gov

rubrics_metrics.name: nation (usage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid the phrase 'the nation's' when referring to a specific country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be specific — e.g., 'Britain’s largest airport' or 'Germany’s largest airport'; avoid the American cliché 'the nation’s capital'. Use 'the U.S. capital' or 'Washington' as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Guard
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize in American usage for U.S. or state forces; lower case for other countries' national guards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories from the United States filed elsewhere should explain the National Guard is a militia force. Examples: 'the National Guard', 'Kansas National Guard'.

rubrics_metrics.name: national names
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not need to specify a minister’s nationality in first paragraph when dateline names the country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under a Washington dateline write 'Secretary of State Joan Smith said ...' rather than 'U.S. Secretary of State...'. Likewise, under an Athens dateline write 'Police arrested' not 'Greek police arrested.'

rubrics_metrics.name: nationalities
rubrics_metrics.description: Write nationalities in full and not abbreviated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: 'U.S.' for United States. Use 'Britain' and 'British' (not United Kingdom or Great Britain). Use 'The Netherlands' (not Holland) and 'Taiwan' (not 'Chinese Taipei'). Distinguish North and South Korea.

rubrics_metrics.name: national security adviser
rubrics_metrics.description: Not an official title: lower case.

rubrics_metrics.name: nationwide
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a head of state/government goes on TV or radio assume nationwide broadcast; specify only if it is not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Native American
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred term for indigenous peoples of the U.S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes Inuit who are not Indians; 'American Indian' is acceptable. Where possible be more specific and give tribe (e.g., Navajo, Cherokee). See 'race' guidance.
